utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you once again of the affirmation that you took, Mr. Jusic. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Petrovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jusic.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My respects to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that on the 5th of December some public address system had been installed on the -- at the JNA positions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, was this the first time that you heard anything of this kind being installed at JNA positions?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the first time. That was at Zarkovica hill and Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your conclusion? How did -- why -- on the basis of what did you conclude that those people on the hill knew what was happening in Dubrovnik and when it was happening?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despite all the hardships that it had experienced, Dubrovnik tried to live a normal cultural life, so that on the 5th, as I already stated in my statement, organised the concert to commemorate the 200th anniversary of Mozart's death, and this was aired on Radio Dubrovnik. So it was nothing underground or secret that this concert was being held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your statement, you also said that on that day, they were playing Serbian nationalist songs.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember exactly what songs, specifically which ones, what kind of songs?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were songs played to the -- sung to the accompaniment of the gusle, and I was familiar with them. I knew them. I had even sung some of them myself, but the texts were -- the lyrics were changed on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what the lyrics were like?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the lyrics of one song. It is a bit vulgar, if the Trial Chamber will allow me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How vulgar? In what way? Do you think, do you feel that the gusle instrument is the test of the cultural level and sophistication of a people?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that every nation has its own, like Dubrovnik has the lijerica which is a string instrument which is typical of Dubrovnik; and in Slavonia they have the tamburica and also the mandolin in Dubrovnik. So every nation has the right to choose its own instruments, but I personally like these songs which were sung with the gusle, which extols Serbian and Montenegrin heroism and valor. It was something which I liked, it was not something which I didn't like or found to be unlikeable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to the 6th of December. The day before yesterday, in response to a question by my colleague, you spoke about the fortissimo of events taking place on the 6th of December, and in that context, you said that on that day in regard -- or, rather, ships and aeroplanes and cannon were opening fire on Dubrovnik. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, were you -- did you record, did you film any aircraft which was operating on that day?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were aircraft flying above because I could recognise them by their sound, and that even had taken place in August and in September. They were flying very low behind my back towards the fort up there, and I am familiar with the sound of a diving plane when it dives, plunges, or when it fires a missile. I'm familiar with those sounds so I could recognise them. And as for the rest, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear on the 6th of December -- this diving of planes sound and the bombing of Srdj?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I also suppose that on that day you saw these gunboats opening fire at the Old Town and the city of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several gunboats. At least four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Be so kind as to tell me, approximately where were -- where were these four gunboats that were opening fire at Dubrovnik on the 6th of Dubrovnik [as interpreted], vis-a-vis Dubrovnik, if you can describe.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I believe that you are familiar with the layout. They were in front of Lokrum and Kupari. For instance, along this stretch one was to the right from Lokrum and another one farther down towards the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me as you were observing them on that day how frequently that they opened fire? At what intervals did you hear the gunboats, did you see the gunboats open fire?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look here, it wasn't exactly such a concentration that I was able to follow the numbers of the firings, but it was quite frequent, and of course I had to see to it that I saved my own life. I wasn't sure whether the gunboat would be opening fire in my direction or elsewhere. One of them did open fire with the projectile landing under my window, and all the panes collapsed. And it is really strange how much glass there can be in a single apartment when it is all shattered and caves in. So I was actually lashed at by these gunboats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your flat was hit on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A shell landed below my window, and there is still a hole in the wall, and all the windows and all the glass in my apartment was shattered, and it fell inside my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you film this damage?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I did, because by comparison, compared to other people's damage, their burnt houses and palaces, it would be quite pitiful on my part to actually concern myself with just that damage which I had sustained. It was impossible to get windowpanes, by the way, but I managed to somehow solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 6th of December, your flat sustained such a serious damage and you did not film it by your camera -- with your camera.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't say it was serious damage. It was damage which was not serious in comparison to the damage sustained by other houses and palaces in Dubrovnik that had been demolished and where much more precious things and objects were. For me it was much more important to record the other damage in the city rather than this pitiful glass in my own flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else happened in your house? Everything was turned upside down, the glass was shattered. What else happened?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have this armchair which I enjoy sitting, smoking, puffing away on my pipe, thinking, so it cut through my -- the glass which fell into the flat cut through the fabric on the armchair exactly where I used to sit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, what did your flat look like after everything?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a shambles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you feel in respect of your flat at that moment? Was this the only damage that had been inflicted on your damage -- on your flat?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, here, the damage which I sustained was spiritual, of an inner nature. This was descending lower into the mud, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, how is it possible that today, after the two statements Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that you made, after the examination-in-chief by my colleague, after my own cross-examination for two days, this is the first time that you mention that your own flat had been hit, that there was damage to your own flat? How is this possible, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, I believe this is actually the first time that the question has been asked. So it's not the subject of an attack on a previous inconsistent statement or previous admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kaufman. Carry on, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Be so kind as to give me an answer. So your life was at risk; shrapnel whizzed by you, hit in the chair where you normally sat, and you never mentioned that throughout all these examinations. How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, that is distorting the evidence given by the witness, obviously unconsciously. There was no mention of shrapnel coming into the apartment, merely of glass being shattered by an explosion. And if a chair was cut, on the evidence so far, it would be glass, not shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you explain to us what was damaged and by what.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep saying that the shell landed in my flat, and you keep seeking to trip me by your additional questions, but I will do my best not to do that. What I said was that the shell landed below my apartment, not in the apartment. There was an explosion. Because of the explosion, the detonation, this pressure shattered all the windows, and there are still many holes on the house facade caused by these lead or iron parts, and one of these iron parts hit my chair and cut through it, and this was perhaps red hot iron. I believe it was red hot, being able to pierce through walls and through the house. So it didn't fall in my flat, in my house, but under my house, below my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this red hot iron, as you put it, was a piece of that shell; right?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if shrapnel hit your flat, your chair, and all but killed you, why didn't you say so? Why didn't you tell it to the investigators? Why didn't you say it to the gentleman from the OTP? Why didn't you tell it to us? We've been talking about all this for three days now.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we have only just broached this subject. And as I said awhile ago, this was not of the essence for me. It was -- but in comparison to the other damage and the other disgrace caused by your army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, please be so kind as to be dignified in this court and refrain from characterising my -- characterisations of the kind "my army," "your army," and the like. So you did not film all of this because thought it unimportant?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not because it was unimportant but because there were other things that were much more important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this hit was from the gunboat; right?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm no expert on weaponry. It was -- shells were flying from every conceivable quarter. There was shooting from every conceivable quarter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you it was on the 6th, as for the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the hour?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It was perhaps midday, 1.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when this happened?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on my balcony at the time, in a corner, huddling in a corner like a mouse, crouching, and filming what was actually going on in my town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were huddling like a mouse in this corner of your balcony and filming. And where is this film, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You saw it. This is the recording of the shooting at Dubrovnik. That is the film.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Jusic, we saw nothing of the kind on that footage, that there was an explosion, a shrapnel passing by, getting inside, passing by your head. Where can we look for it?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't view it carefully, obviously. Please don't mind my saying so, but you can see precisely on the footage how this grapevine leaves climbing up my balcony are there. You can see how I'm thrown back by the pressure of the detonation and, therefore, the whole picture changes. All this was obvious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was the exact moment when the shrapnel flew into your flat?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The shells were landing, and the nearer the shells landed, the more pressure was exerted on me by the air, the detonating air. Whether it was that precise moment, I'm not sure, but you can see me veering at that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, the moment when this fracas took place, when the shrapnel flew into your flat, this was filmed?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't turned towards my flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But -- but your camera was on at the moment when this was happening.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I was recording Dubrovnik. I was filming Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at no point you turned this camera to film what had happened in the -- in your flat. Your -- the camera didn't just fall out of your hand. Nothing happened. You tottered a bit but you continued filming Dubrovnik; is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was this explosion of this shell from your flat?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 25 metres to the right from my flat, under my balcony. It hit a tall palm tree, which you can see on the footage. I filmed it before but I didn't film it afterwards when just the trunk remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it destroyed, demolished?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just the trunk remained of the palm tree. The crown was knocked off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How high up is your balcony in relation to that palm tree?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are more or less the same, but perhaps the palm tree is a bit higher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the shell hit the palm tree.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the house that is underneath mine, and that's where a man got killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A man in that house underneath my window got killed by one of the shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't consider that to be important enough to tell the investigators?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honey, I'm answering your questions. You didn't ask me that. Ask me, and I'll tell you everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to my learned friend Mr. Kaufman's question, you were telling us the day before yesterday about the month of October. Mr. Kaufman didn't ask you anything, and you said that in the month of October, a shell from the gunboat hit the apartment of the poet Milisic and he got killed by that.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is to my left, the palm tree is to the right, and Dubrovnik is in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just trying to explain the position to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether it's left or right. Mr. Kaufman did not ask you anything, and you told him, "I want to tell you about the poet Milisic," and now you're telling us that nobody asked you about the shrapnel flying around your apartment, and you're surprised and you say, "Nobody asked me about this." Well, nobody asked you about Milisic either and nevertheless you talked about it.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen, sir; you're somewhat younger than I am, and I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. imagine that you will learn this some day. In life, there are things that are important, very important, of utmost importance, and of lesser importance. I talked about the most important things that were happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This man who was killed by a shell that flew into your apartment too, isn't that the most important? Is he as important as any other person who got killed?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I didn't know his name. Later on, I learned his name. Later on, I also learned that his two young children were orphaned and that his wife was widowed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't this tragedy make you feel that you should talk about that too? It happened below your very own window.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, when these investigators came to see me and when I talked to Mr. Kaufman, I was told that I would basically talk about the cultural damage sustained by Dubrovnik, and that is what I chose to talk about too. If you're interested in anything, please go ahead and ask me about it. I am prepared to answer your questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you once again: Are you sure that this was on the 6th of December? Please give me an honest answer. Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please don't use the word "honest." Of course I'm going to give an honest answer. Perhaps I'll get confused about some dates. I don't know if you were ever in a situation when there was shooting all around you and when you did not know whether you would survive the next moment or so. I think that this is too unfair, let's put it that way. Because Dubrovnik was not attacked only on the 6th. It was also attacked in November and then also a few times in 2002 [as interpreted]. So I cannot give you the precise days and hours. So my answer is: I don't want to lie to you, I am giving an answer, and I'm not quite -- I always tell you I'm not sure about something, but this what I talked about now happened on the 6th for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If I were to tell you that this was perhaps in 1992, when the town was also attacked, is it possible that it happened then? Because there were very serious attacks that took place in May and June, more serious than the ones that we're talking about now.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why are you asking me that when you know better?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether it is possible.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but this thing with my window happened on the 6th. That's for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, please, how could you tell from which direction shells were coming?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the gunboats. I saw them, and that can be seen on the film too. So when it fires a shell, there is a lot of smoke. On the eastern side, from Zarkovica and Bosanka, that is so nearby it is as if somebody came right to your ear and then caused an explosion. Some shells travelled quite long or, rather, I think that they came from the airport, or people were saying that they were coming from the airport or Trebinje. And this is my feeling, especially in view of my musical ear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us distinguish between the two. I'm not asking you about what you saw on films, video footage, and whatever. I'm asking you about what you heard on that particular day. I did not ask you about what you saw on videotape and then assessed it this way or that way. What was your judgement then on that day? What was coming from where?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I am sure that I put this very precisely. I told you that I saw them shooting from the gunboat. I heard this shooting from Bosanka Zarkovica because it was so nearby, and then by their sound I could tell that some shells were coming from afar. So I think that I've been very precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you distinguish between firing and detonation? Can you distinguish between the two? Do you know what the difference is?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that on the first day. Firing is a single thing, and then when a shell would fall, there would be 15 or 20 reverberations. You couldn't tell where it was coming from; the sky, the land. That's what I talked about the first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why can firing not be heard in that way too?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it probably comes from a forest. It is camouflaged, so there is not enough space for this sound to develop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which forest? Do you know which one?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Zarkovica and Bosanka are forested, and then also behind the hills, too, there are forests. It's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any forests in Lapad, Babin Kuk, Ilijina Glavica, Gradac?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogisica Park?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are pine trees, and there are Cyprus trees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard firing and then you would hear 15 reverberations of the detonation that was caused by the firing?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very acoustic. It's acoustics: Dom, dom, dom, dom. That's it. It's as if somebody had spilled something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of it came from a single shell?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but if I understand this properly, from one or two shells one had the impression that this was a burst of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One had the impression that it was hell, that it was inferno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the sound of firing is as far as a mortar is concerned?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No idea whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the sound of a howitzer firing is?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now that you mention all these words, please don't judge me too harshly, but when you say "howitzer," it sounds so serious. It must be a very serious sound that comes when it's fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a cannon?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you put it, "top," as you said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that is the word for cannon in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a recoilless gun? How does that sound?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never saw any such thing. Never heard it. Only saw it in the movies. I think there was this film made by Montenegrin television as young men were firing proudly from this so-called recoilless gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you watch any films from Dubrovnik with this kind of content, describing the war in 1997 -- sorry, 1991?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean from Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: HTV, for instance, Croatian television.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, I have to tell you one thing; the HTV cannot pride itself at having been present in Dubrovnik. We did a lot more filming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What with Vedran Benic, a friend of yours that you mentioned yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vedran Benic used my music when he made this film about the Imperijal Fortress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of film is this about the Imperijal Fortress?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He shot a film which tells the truth about this fortress. It tells its history, not only the history today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you watched this film?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I was not in Dubrovnik then. I know that he wanted to have my music as a sound track because it made it more dramatic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps ask him what he said about recent events - not so recent any longer; 1991, 1992 - in that film?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you interested in how your music was used in that film?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, he's my friend, and let me draw a parallel line straight away. A friend of mine from Belgrade called me about ten years ago or more, and he asked me, "Can I use your song Dok Palme Njisu Grane so that it could be used as part of the Partizan football team anthem?" And I said, "Yes, that's fine." So it's being played and sung until the present day. I like that team, the black and white team. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is that the film that dates back to 1994?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Benic's film, the one we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact year. Look, it is 2004 now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on the 6th of December you recorded everything that is of importance on your tape, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did record what was of importance to me; the palaces, the festival building, old institutions, cultural institutions. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please focus on my question. I'm asking you the following: Is it correct that on the 6th of December you recorded everything that you considered to be of importance, on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, on the footage, you saw that people who were in the streets, if there were any at all, they were walking right by the walls. I walked right by the walls too. Even if I wanted to, I could not have come closer to many of the buildings that I wanted to come close to. So there was a state of alert on and it was possible for a shell to fall even then. It is a personal risk I took, and that is how I displayed my love for my town, and even at the risk of my own life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you filmed this on the 6th of December, when was that other footage shot when we can see that there were shells falling in the old part of town?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th. I entered the town on the 7th, sir. I entered the town on the 7th and recorded all of this. We resolved that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We did not resolve that. You keep telling me about all these things that happened on the 7th. I'm asking you about the 6th.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th I'm on my balcony and I'm filming Dubrovnik, and we saw that. First we watched the 7th, and then we watched the 6th. So I could not have been in two places at the same time. On the 6th I'm filming the town from the balcony, and on the 7th I'm in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you for the third time.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 6th of December you recorded everything that was of importance on your tape?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my balcony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I filmed where the shells fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you film everything that you considered to be of importance?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around midday, I ran out of batteries, so then I was filming until, say, midday or 1.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps recall telling us yesterday that around 12.00 or 1.00 you stopped filming and then you recharged your battery so that you'd have it for the next day?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's not what I said. I said that sometimes I would stop so that my batteries would not run out, but I said that that day I filmed for as long as I could, but then I said that I raced over to Revelin or some other building where there was electricity in order to recharge my battery, and I went normally when there was no curfew. Of course I remember what we talked about yesterday, the day before yesterday. I remember that very well. And it's going to be very hard for you to trip me this way, but it's your job to try to set these traps for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fortunately, Mr. Jusic, there is a transcript. So on the 6th, when did you go to recharge that battery?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime after 5.00 or 6.00, something like that. Something like that. And that's when the shelling stopped too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you recharge it? You didn't tell us.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Fort Revelin. That is on the right-hand side as soon as you enter town. They had a generator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did police vehicles ever enter the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police vehicles? No. No. No. Definitely not, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in relation to Pavo Urban, what do you know about this young man's death? How do you know about this? How come you know about it at all?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be seen from the last photographs taken exactly where he was. And then his mother, who is nearby on her window, and she saw her child being killed. That's how I know. And I knew the young man as an incredibly brave young man who went all over the place and took photographs. He made some beautiful photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So his mother watched his death from her window. Where does his mother live?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His mother lives somewhere, say, in Zudioska or Boskoviceva, in that area. That's one or two streets in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from Zudioska Street she saw her son being killed?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say Zudioska. It's between Zudioska and Boskoviceva. I cannot say exactly. I know approximately the window where these people live, and I know the man who ran across the street and recovered his body from Dubrovacko-Neretvljanska but it was too late.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the Dubrovnik Zupanija was established? Briefly. If you don't know, you don't know.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Probably after the first elections because that is when these Zupanija districts were established.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First it was in the City Hall, now it is across the street from the Rector's Palace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Old Town, right?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the county governor, the head of the Zupanija in this period?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was Dr. Jure Buric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Buric play any role in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He played no role. In fact, I don't know. I never saw him at any specific meetings or consultations. He is a doctor. He is a specialist in otorhinolaryngology - ear, nose, and throat specialist - and he was elected in Dubrovnik at the legal elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true what you told us the other day -- excuse me. I withdraw my question. Tell me, awhile ago you said that everything which was important on the 6th of December you filmed. Now, tell me, how much tape did you use up on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday that I used one whole tape and a part of another, a VHS tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I'm adding up numbers well, you told us you used 120 tapes.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said I was using 60 tapes, 120 tapes, and I'd given up the 240 ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one did you use on that day?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe 120.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other one, what was it?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I filmed a birthday, a birthday celebration with me and my friends partying, and it is about ten or 15 minutes, and there was some space still left on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 6th of December, this is how much tape you spent.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. We were watching this car, and I had been using it to film from November. It was not only in December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's try again. How much tape did you use on the 6th of December? For how long were you filming? How long was the camera on?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean minutes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hours, minutes, whatever.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on. The camera was on for two hours or two and a half hours, as long as the battery -- until the battery expired. You know what? From time to time I would seek shelter. I'm not that much of a hero. I was not standing on my balcony all the time. I fled occasionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for two hours and a half. All right. Since from the 6th of December, on the tape which was shown to the Trial Chamber, you have nine minutes and 25 seconds of that particular data. Tell me, where are the two hours and 21 minutes of material that you filmed on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you keep talking about the minutes and hours. I never said that I filmed for all that time. I just said that one tape lasted for 15 minutes and the other for a certain period of time which doesn't add up to two hours more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that two -- five minutes ago, but two minutes ago I asked you how much did you film, for how long did you film that day, and you replied, "For two and a half hours." This is page 27 -- 20, line 17.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is one thing how much I was standing on the balcony and how much I was actually filming. You asked me how long was the camera continuously on. Well, I would turn the camera on and off. This is the type I spent on the balcony. But I cannot say exactly I was filming for an hour and fifteen minutes or so. There were interruptions. I would run inside for some refreshments, for a drink, then I would return, to get back to normal, that is. So it was not a continuous two and a half hours filming. That is why there cannot be that much material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much material did you film on the 6th of December? Let us not waste our time in this manner. We are under the obligation to go through this as quickly as possible. How much material in terms of time, in terms of duration, did you film on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably filled one tape, but then I edited the interruptions, the pauses, so that I actually omitted the pauses in the final version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, where is this material which you so edited?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I invited you to come to Dubrovnik for us to view this tape together, and this invitation still stands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So everything which is important is within the nine minutes and 21 seconds -- 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything which is the most important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What falls within the category of important things?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is important, what is the most important for a house flying into the air, being blown up, to be seen. It is the most important for the Festival Palace to be seen ablaze, that the St. Blaise Church has been demolished, there is a hole in the Stradun, that all the gates of the town have been devastated, that there is a hole in the bell tower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps need a pause, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is about the 6th of December. This is what I keep insisting on while you're telling me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: It appears that the witness is in the middle of an answer, giving a detailed list of buildings that he saw in a state of damage or ablaze. Mr. Petrovic is cutting him off in the middle of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if Mr. Petrovic hadn't, I would have. We're finding this very difficult, Mr. Jusic. You have two relevant filming days, the 6th of December and the 7th of December. On the 7th of December, as I understand your evidence, you went about the Old Town and identified and recorded various buildings of significance that were damaged and some general other scenes. On the 6th of December, we have only a few minutes of actual footage which we have seen here. What Mr. Petrovic is trying to find out is what else was it that you recorded on the 6th of December rather than on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No. This is really likable, this congenial conversation where, you know, dribbling like football, like soccer players. I said decidedly that I filmed over a period of two and a half hours on the 6th of December and that after that I just edited out the big pauses, the interruptions in the film between the two shells or between my going to get a drink of water and to, you know, keep body and soul together, restore myself to a normal state. That was on the 6th. And on the 7th I regained my composure and very calmly toured my city with my camera, and that is what I show on that film, because I was only interested in the devastation of the cultural facilities and monuments in the city. And this is what I very precisely showed and said. And whether it was a minute more, a minute less, I think is immaterial. I really invited, in the best of faith, Mr. Petrovic to come to my city so that we can together tour it. We can travel today, I to my city, he to his and one day we can together see what happened there. This is what I sought to show in this movie, the most important things. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, that brings me back to the 6th of December. We have only a few minutes of footage. Is that the only footage you took of shells exploding and similar things on the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible that there were some things which are of a lesser importance, but that is why I'm offering this possibility for us to view once again this film, everything that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that, but we're concerned with what is here, and we're trying to understand what else you filmed on the 6th that is not shown on the footage that is here. At the moment from you, it seems that there are passages where there was interruption and in-between stuff of no significance, and perhaps you added then at the end that there may be some amount of material that showed more of the attack on the city. Is that about it or is there something new and different that you filmed on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I said very precisely that there are some less important things. These things were the more important for me. What I'm saying is no one forced me, no one compelled me, no one paid me nor engaged me to film that. No one actually compelled me to come to testify before this distinguished Chamber. This is all a question of my goodwill as a man who wants to tell the truth in keeping with the affirmation that I have made, that I will indeed be saying the whole truth and nothing but. And if Mr. Petrovic would acknowledge that I'm saying the truth and I have only filmed what I thought was the most important to be presented in this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic has a role to perform on behalf of his client, and he's been trying to understand the difference between the few minutes of footage that we do have and your account that you could have been filming for over two hours, and that is what he is doing. Now, Mr. Petrovic, I think we may have just about exhausted this area. The Chamber is well aware of the differences between the footage and the accounts of the amount of filming that occurred on the 6th, and that's what is of significance for your purposes, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many shells landed, how many hits on the Old Town were there on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the number, but at this moment in Dubrovnik, on the east side at the gate to the city, you have a layout of the city, as well as on the west side, and you have all these impact sites indicated by black marks. I believe that they have it here in the archives. I could not tell by the just sound of the shells how many thousands or hundreds of them there had been, but there were very many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were many -- several hundreds or thousands?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not thousands but let us say, you know in all fairness, a thousand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all this refers to the Old Town; right?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I suppose that if not all of them -- all of it, you filmed most of it.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, when there is a house being demolished, flying into the air, now as you can see on the footage very nicely, I really cannot tell whether it was caused by one or two or five shells, but it was inferno. Don't ask me to give you any expert answers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for any expert opinions. I'm just asking you whether you filmed most of it or all of it.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did. I had to react. I turned my camera on when I saw it and I filmed it. I didn't have a, you know, a camera on a tripod. I had -- I carried it on my shoulder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you be surprised, Mr. Jusic, when I tell you the following: At 3.58 hours, one shot was filmed. I'm referring to the time indicated on your tape. So 3:58. At 4:18, a hit south from the Stradun was -- is on your film. At 4:34, you have filmed smoke billowing above Srdj. At 6:18, you have filmed two impacts to the south of the Stradun. At 7:25, you have an impact on the music school. At 10:14, a hit in the area of the music school. At 11:35, a hit in the area of the Stradun or to the north of Stradun. And at 13:07, you filmed a shell falling either in the general area of Stradun or to the south of Stradun. Mr. Jusic, you filmed nine impacts of shells landing in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what is the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that you actually filmed the impacts of nine shells landing in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what? Dubrovnik is an amalgamation of beauty, tradition, centuries-old culture. It is as if you had a beautiful girl and just tore off a nail from her finger. It wouldn't be the same girl any more. When you say -- when you refer to these nine impacts, this is terrible. This is disastrous, you know, to throw nine shells on such a beautiful girl and set afire nine mansions. I said awhile ago that you have an indication at the entry to the city of exactly how many shells had landed on the city, which is confirmed by the United Nations, by UNESCO. So it is not a falsehood. And had I just filmed one of them falling, that would have been sufficient. It would have been a shame to throw stones at this beautiful lady let alone shells. That is what I'm saying to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you filmed the nine, but nine is too much.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is too much. It is way too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask Ms. McCreath if she can help me now. Would you kindly show the -- from the first part of the tape minute 3 -- the third minute and ten seconds, that is. If it's not a problem, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, can you see this picture in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the gunboat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when was this filmed?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, here. These gunboats moved about for two or three months. So this is a bit too much. You're asking me a bit too much, because they were there for at least three months, you know, cruising up and down and -- by Dubrovnik and opening fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you edit this film in a chronological sequence?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no. I just provided information. I wasn't thinking like a director, like a movie director. I was just -- my only consideration was to show these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't have -- the clips are not in chronological sequence?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even think about it. I don't know whether it is in chronological sequence or not. My only consideration was to show as many things as possible, to show the gunboats, to show the shelling, for the shells to be heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see this gunboat just opened fire. You can see the smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you see this smoke?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right from the captain's bridge. That is smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there is one that is smoking, and we'll come to that eventually. So from this multitude of materials that you had, you cut it out, added it, edited. There is no chronology on the tape. So I can conclude that what you wrote happened on the 6th, indicated as having happened on the 6th, perhaps was the shelling of the Old City which took place either earlier or later?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot. That only took place on the 6th, and that is the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you say now that it is only the 6th, 6th when repeatedly to questions put to you by Mr. Kaufman you said that when you were filming the automobile, from your balcony, flying into the air, that didn't take place on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. I remembered that that took place in November, but the shelling of the city is only on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know about this gunboat, when this was taken?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be before or afterwards, but I'm telling you, they were there for at least three months, and they were shooting at random, not in a planned fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, would you please be so kind as to explain the logic of the film to me. How did you organise this? Why does the car come first and then the gunboat? I mean, if it's not chronological. Did you do it in the order of importance or whatever?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sort of. I started thinking, this car was in November and then comes the 6th, the attack, the shelling; and then comes the 7th when I went to town. This gunboat was around Dubrovnik a month before that and a month or two after that. And not only this one but four or five of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask Ms. McCreath to show us 15 minutes and 40 seconds, for instance. And then I'm going to ask for the tape to be stopped at a particular point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you stop now, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, you entered town; isn't that right? Now we're already on the 7th of December?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we in Stradun now?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, Stradun, the beginning, on the eastern side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we see quite a few people in Stradun on that day?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Way too many for that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When was this filmed, at what time?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please move on to the seventeenth minute, 30 seconds, 35 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Could you play it very slowly now. Just go on slowly forward if that's no problem. Stop now, please. Stop. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see this car, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the blue licence plate on this car, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. It's a bit dim, but I can see that it's blue, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose licence plate is this, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see well because it's very dim. It's out of focus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to tell the Trial Chamber who had blue licence plates in the Republic of Croatia, in the SFRY at the time we're discussing. Whose vehicles had blue licence plates only?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think it was the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a bit further. Can you see this blue vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose vehicles were blue, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my last car, the one before last, was blue, and now I have a red car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, no doubt you're a very witty man.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you. This blue vehicle with blue licence plates, who does it belong to?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, there were different licence plates in Dubrovnik at the time. There were international licence plates. I can't tell you whose it is. I can't see very well. It is true that it is blue, yes, but I also see that there are white seats, and I never saw the police with white seats in their cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, a blue vehicle with blue M licence plates, is that a police car? Yes or no. Just give me a brief answer.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you don't know.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why it would N. What do you mean N?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean M, meaning the police on blue licence plates. That's the only such thing that existed in the Republic of Croatia and the SFRY, the one and only.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ours were called police with a P, Policija, not M, Milicija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Jusic. In 1991, the police in Croatia was called Milicija with an M, like everywhere else in the former Yugoslavia, but let's not go into all that now. Tell me, where was this filmed, in front of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got out of the municipality. I was filming until about 1 -- until about 9.00 and then I went to the municipality to recharge my battery because they have a generator too. And now we'll see what the time is because I happened to film that as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this vehicle filmed in front of the municipality next to the Rector's Palace opposite St. Blaise Church?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move a bit forward, 17:56 or, rather, 17:50. Could you please play the tape now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Stop. Just a bit further. Thank you. Can we see the whole clip, please. Just a bit further. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are those people, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good question. Good question. I wanted to ask you that. Again the siren went off around 10.00. So this is a state of alert, and people have fled to shelters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that you did not change the sequence here either?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Can I suggest that within the next half minute I know I'm going to ask a passerby what day is it today, as if I knew you'd be asking me this some day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I remember that. It is fifteen to twelve.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty to twelve. Twenty minutes before midday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell me, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If we could intrude, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Jusic, there appears to be a lengthy shadow across the street thrown by a building. Can you -- would you agree that the sunrises at about 7.00 in the morning at that time of the year in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. What we see now is twenty minutes to twelve, so you can see the shadow of the sun. This is not 7.00 in the morning. This is twenty to twelve, this particular clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what time would you say the sunrises at that time in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think around 6.30 or 7.00, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you see anything unusual about the extent of shadow that's cast, or is that what you would expect near midday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This shadow that can be seen here is the street, the street that is intersected by the sun. And then as the sun goes further, it includes other streets. So that's why this looks this way. But if you allow me, this street is otherwise as smooth as a mirror, and I see how it is riddled with shrapnel bullets, hits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. We interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, how many buildings exactly burned on the 6th of December, as you had put it? What is the actual number?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's start with the festival building. That's one. And then this other building before the festival building. That is another palace, so that's number two. And then the house where Ivo Grbic, the well-known artist, lives, that's number 3. Then the house next door is number 4. And then that palace is number 5. And then two palaces vis-a-vis the Orthodox church. That's 7, right. Then near the Sorkocevic building, that's 8. I filmed that. And I'm not including those holes. I'm talking about houses that were burned to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, on your footage, six can be seen. Out of them, two buildings that you refer to can be seen only partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. McCreath, can we see minutes 26, please, 32 -- 26 minutes 20 seconds, approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the building --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please let me put the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop now, please, just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Grbic's house, the house of the painter Grbic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is the shop of the Belgrade ready-made clothing factory on the ground floor of his house? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can agree with that, yes. Grbic lived upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move a bit further on, minute number 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop now, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come this sign, this lamp, was intact? What's it made of?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, please don't mind my saying so, but this is a crazy question. I mean, come on. How can you say that? Something just happens to remain intact. I mean, it's just by accident. How did I manage to survive? By chance. Your Honour, please. Please be so kind as to -- don't allow him to put this kind of questions to me. They are not fair. They are not proper, after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, I can well understand that you feel very deeply some of these things, but a question like that can be shortly and simply answered, "By chance," and that's all you need to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please play a bit further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what it looked like. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is a shop of the Titograd ready-made clothing factory housed in this building?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I see it says Titex Boutique. Well, obviously a shell fell straight on the house, and obviously these two lamps that are outside were protected by the walls. And it is really sensational that they remained intact. Obviously the shell fell on the house, not next to the house. Now that I'm composed, I can explain that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you was: Is this the -- the store that belonged to the Titograd ready-made clothing factory?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just see the words Boutique Titex. I don't know who it belongs to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have minute 29 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop now, please. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is another one of the houses that were burned.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a palace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a palace. Can you see in the lower left-hand corner this logo?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the Kluz logo, again a Belgrade manufacturer.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we see it a bit better? Can it be focused? Perhaps it's Kluc. It's not that I'm trying to deny what you're saying, but it may be Kluc, not necessarily Kluz.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. McCreath, can we focus this a bit? Can we zoom in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. [Interpretation] What did you say that was written here?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said Kluz.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a Z at the end. I couldn't decipher that. What about this dot on the Z if it is a Z?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are ways of checking this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see minute 30 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these are three buildings. Could you please stop the tape now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a fourth brigade that burned down. It's the one opposite the Serbian Orthodox Church.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't that a bit strange that out of the six buildings that burned down, four, or at least three, were Serb buildings?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if that question is not requesting speculation from the witness. I would object on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have an answer to the question, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. I do, and I'd be glad to give this answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, these were buildings from the former Yugoslavia. Secondly, they're on the ground floor, but then upstairs there were Croats who were living there. It was Croat citizens that were hit. And this says even more about the attackers. They just wanted to devastate Dubrovnik indiscriminately, and they succeeded at that point in time. They did not discriminate between faiths or ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we're just about right on time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, deeply aware of what you said to me yesterday, I nevertheless have to say that I faced considerable problems in terms of obtaining answers to the questions I put, so I do apologise, and could I please have another 15 minutes after this break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll make it ten minutes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And this is the time when we need to break. We will have the normal break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, how many hits to the pavement of the Stradun did you film?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I exactly filmed the pavement of the street, but I did see that it was riddled, and there were some parts of it that were devastated, slabs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You filmed two, one before the -- in front of the Festival Palace, the other in Palmoticeva Street.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many more, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many hits did you film or how many hits were there around the Orlando's column?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I concretely filmed two holes, a large hole, a smaller one, and one was on the Church of the Saint -- of St. Blaise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the pavement.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, the pavement. I filmed two holes in front of St. Blaise's Church, near Orlando's pillar or column.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask Mrs. McCreath for us to go to the thirty-fifth minute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before we do that, can you tell me, you filmed also the damage to the Franciscan cloister; right?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I'm not wrong, you also filmed the damage sustained in the refectory of the cloister.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe somebody was explaining to you which way the shell landed and how it entered the room.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what it exploded?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who is doing the explaining is the superior of the monastery, the guardian. His name is Mato Polonio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, all right. What did he tell you? Where did it explode?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He showed me with his hand where it had come in through the window and it could have only come from Bosanka or Zarkovica, this projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, did he describe to you where it had exploded inside the room or --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you think, in view of the damage?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it exploded up on the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you now let us see the 35th minute, 12th second. The 35th minute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the superior --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please wait until I put the question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you go back a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please explain how come that everything else -- everything remained in its proper place in this room when the explosion took place so near? You can see the pitcher with water, you can see the chair. How was it possible?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that it exploded up on the window, not inside. Had it exploded inside, the damage would have been far greater. Fortunately, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is this window from this pitcher of water, for instance?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some five metres up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nothing happened to the pitcher from an explosion which was five metres away?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honey, it did not explode inside. It exploded five metres away on the window and these are pieces of the window. So this window was above the superior, where he was showing to me the place, not above the pitcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for going back a bit, but could we go back a bit to the -- to 24 minutes and 30 seconds, please. A bit more, please. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this motorbiker who was driving down the Stradun out of spite, as you put it, what does this car mean? What is that? Who is that, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was -- this was total anarchy or, rather, people were driving around out of protest. I don't know what exactly it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The end of the 24th minute, please. Go back a bit. Towards the facade. Yes. Now -- stop now, please. And a few frames back again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does this bell tower face?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wanted precisely --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the -- in the cardinal points, the left side, the insulated side.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The flag faces the east, and to the left is the west. Up there is the north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now you've been telling us persistently for three days that the shells had been coming from the direction of the east. Now, where do you see on the east side of the cupola this damage that you say came from the east?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I remember vividly. I'm sure it was a shell from the Bosanka or Zarkovica. This is precisely the stretch towards Zarkovica, and you can see this hole. That is exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was all from the east side.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is from the east side. This is still the east side, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are certain that the east side of this building is damaged?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drew on the map where Zarkovica is, but I can perhaps say that it was north-east, but it was from Zarkovica that the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall we now go, please, to 40. Your Honour, I'm compelled to give up a large number of my questions but that will be the subject of our written submissions when the time comes. So let us go to the 43rd minute, 33rd second. Run the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A bit forward, please. Yes, this is it. Thank you. Stop please. A couple of seconds back, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see this gunboat, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that it had just fired its projectile, and this is the smoke which shows that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the very end of your tape.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that's the end of my tape, but this is the gunboat which had just opened fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the 43rd minute of the 44 that your tape has.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And what do you need from me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I need you to tell me when you filmed this.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This gunboat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact hour but the fact is it is opening fire at Dubrovnik. This is the most important thing for me, that it is opening fire at Dubrovnik, and at me, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is important that it is opening fire at you and at Dubrovnik and the date is not important, in your opinion?
